items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had seen his band the last week they were in existence - when he had Miles Davis and Doug Mettome in the trumpet section at the Regal Theater.

ctx.x: So Dizzy was known for of course being one of the fathers of - of course ­ bebop, but he seemed to be very active in promoting this music to youth. Was he engaged in any way with you and helping, giving youth access to this music and helping them understand, or at least see the value of this music?

Well I don’t know except that he came up to our sessions and he also played for me at the North Park, which was open to all ages. He also played for me down on Rush Street. They had a 25th Anniversary of my promoting, and he was a guest, and he played there, along with the Pieces of Eight, which is an eight piece big little band, little big band. He was always very, very friendly. There’s a picture of us together that has been published around here and there. I never got in to talking about music that much with…
